userStories.title: The run temp wipe survives read-only trees
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `removeRunTmpTree(path)` to `run-tmp-wipe.ts`: on an `EACCES`/`EPERM` failure it walks the tree with `lstat`, gives each directory owner `rwx`, never touches symlinks or anything outside `path`, and retries `rm` once; `wipeRunTmp` removes through it, keeping its logging contract.

**Motivation** — One host held 567 leftover run roots (28 GB) under `/tmp/nax`; a root that a test suite left with a `0500` directory survives `rm -rf` (`EACCES`).

**Approach** — Removal goes through one exported helper, `removeRunTmpTree(path)`, in `execution/lifecycle/run-tmp-wipe.ts`:

1. `rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true })`.
2. On an error whose `code` is `EACCES` or `EPERM`: walk the tree under `path` with `lstat`, which never follows a symlink. Give each directory owner `rwx` (`mode | 0o700`) through `chmod`. Never chmod a symlink or anything outside `path`. Then call `rm` once more.
3. If the retry fails, the error propagates to the caller. Any other first error propagates unchanged without a retry.

`wipeRunTmp(runId)` keeps its contract (absence logged at debug, failure logged at warn and swallowed, `dryRun` skips) and calls `removeRunTmpTree` instead of the bare `rm`.

Failure handling: rm fails with EACCES/EPERM and retry succeeds -> root removed, nothing logged at warn. Retry also fails -> `removeRunTmpTree` rejects; `wipeRunTmp` logs `Failed to wipe run temp dir <path> — continuing` at warn and resolves. rm fails with any other code -> no chmod walk, no retry; the error propagates. `chmod` fails on one directory during the walk -> the walk continues; the retry decides the outcome. `lstat` or `readdir` fails on an entry during the walk -> that entry is skipped; the walk continues and the retry decides the outcome.

**Scope** — In: `removeRunTmpTree`, `_runTmpWipeDeps` extension, `wipeRunTmp` rewiring, existing wipe unit tests updated. Out: the sweep and `closeRunTmp` (US-002); removing the wipe from `cleanupRun` (US-006). Also out: per-session temp wipes.

**Interface**
```typescript
// packages/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-tmp-wipe.ts
export function removeRunTmpTree(path: string): Promise<void>;
export function wipeRunTmp(runId: string, opts?: WipeRunTmpOptions): Promise<void>; // same signature and logging
// _runTmpWipeDeps baseline: { remove, exists }
// _runTmpWipeDeps target:   { remove, exists, lstat, chmod, readdir }  // lstat/chmod/readdir are the node:fs/promises calls the walk uses
```
acceptanceCriteria: With a real temp tree `<root>/a/b/file` where `<root>/a/b` has mode `0o500`, calling `removeRunTmpTree(<root>)` resolves and `<root>` no longer exists.
With a real temp tree whose nested directory has mode `0o500`, calling `wipeRunTmp(<runId>)` (with `runTmpRoot` resolving to that tree) leaves no root and records no warn-level log entry.

With a real temp tree holding a nested `0o500` directory (so the first `rm` fails with `EACCES`) and a symlink `<root>/link` to a directory outside `<root>` whose mode is `0o500`, calling `removeRunTmpTree(<root>)` removes `<root>` and the link target's mode is still `0o500` afterwards.

With a real temp tree holding a nested `0o500` directory and a symlink to a directory outside `<root>` that contains a file, `removeRunTmpTree(<root>)` leaves the link target directory and its file in place.
When `_runTmpWipeDeps.remove` rejects first with an error whose `code` is `EACCES` and then resolves, `removeRunTmpTree` calls `remove` exactly twice.

When `_runTmpWipeDeps.remove` rejects first with an error whose `code` is `EPERM`, `removeRunTmpTree` calls `_runTmpWipeDeps.chmod` on each directory the `lstat` walk reports, each with a mode that includes `0o700`.
When the walk's `lstat` reports an entry as a symbolic link, `removeRunTmpTree` never passes that entry's path to `_runTmpWipeDeps.chmod`.
When `_runTmpWipeDeps.remove` rejects first with an error whose `code` is `ENOTDIR`, `removeRunTmpTree` rejects with that error and calls `remove` exactly once.
When `_runTmpWipeDeps.remove` rejects with `EACCES` on both calls, `removeRunTmpTree` rejects with the second error.
When `_runTmpWipeDeps.chmod` rejects for one directory during the walk, `removeRunTmpTree` still calls `remove` a second time.

When `_runTmpWipeDeps.remove` rejects with `EACCES` on both calls, `wipeRunTmp` resolves, has called `remove` exactly twice, and logs one warn entry whose message is `Failed to wipe run temp dir <path> — continuing`.
When `_runTmpWipeDeps.remove` rejects first with `EACCES` and `_runTmpWipeDeps.readdir` rejects for one directory during the walk, `removeRunTmpTree` still calls `remove` a second time.

routing.reasoning: One source file plus tests; permission-restoring walk with symlink safety, standard injectable-deps pattern.

modifiedFiles.reason: tests that stub `_runTmpWipeDeps.remove` to reject with an `EACCES` error and assert the single warn now go through the permission-restoring retry first; they stub `lstat`/`readdir`/`chmod` (or make the retry reject too) and still assert one `Failed to wipe run temp dir` warn when the retry fails.

userStories.title: runtime.close() removes its run temp root and sweeps stale roots
acceptanceCriteria: `STALE_RUN_TMP_MAX_AGE_MS` imported from `execution/lifecycle/run-tmp-sweep` equals `172800000`.
`sweepStaleRunTmpRoots({ currentRunId: "cur", now, maxAgeMs })` lists the directory `dirname(runTmpRoot("cur"))` through `_runTmpSweepDeps.readdir`.

When the parent holds a directory whose own `mtimeMs` and every direct child's `mtimeMs` are older than `now - maxAgeMs`, `sweepStaleRunTmpRoots` passes that directory's path to `_runTmpSweepDeps.remove`.
When the parent holds an old directory with one direct child whose `mtimeMs` is newer than `now - maxAgeMs`, `sweepStaleRunTmpRoots` does not pass that directory to `_runTmpSweepDeps.remove`.

When the parent holds an old directory whose name equals `basename(runTmpRoot(currentRunId))` for a `currentRunId` containing a character `runTmpRoot` sanitises (for example `a/b`), `sweepStaleRunTmpRoots` does not pass it to `_runTmpSweepDeps.remove`.
When `_runTmpSweepDeps.lstat` reports a parent entry as a symbolic link, `sweepStaleRunTmpRoots` does not pass it to `_runTmpSweepDeps.remove`.
When `_runTmpSweepDeps.lstat` reports a parent entry as a regular file, `sweepStaleRunTmpRoots` does not pass it to `_runTmpSweepDeps.remove`.
When `_runTmpSweepDeps.readdir` rejects with `ENOENT`, `sweepStaleRunTmpRoots` resolves without logging at warn.
When `_runTmpSweepDeps.readdir` rejects with `EACCES`, `sweepStaleRunTmpRoots` resolves and logs exactly one warn entry.

When `_runTmpSweepDeps.remove` rejects for the first of two stale directories, `sweepStaleRunTmpRoots` still passes the second to `remove` and logs one warn entry whose message starts with `Failed to sweep stale run temp dir`.
The default `_runTmpSweepDeps.remove` is `removeRunTmpTree` from `execution/lifecycle/run-tmp-wipe`.
`closeRunTmp({ runId: "r1", dryRun: false })` calls `_runTmpCloseDeps.wipeRunTmp` with `"r1"` before it calls `_runTmpCloseDeps.sweepStaleRunTmpRoots`.

`closeRunTmp({ runId: "r1", dryRun: false })` calls `_runTmpCloseDeps.sweepStaleRunTmpRoots` with `currentRunId: "r1"`, `maxAgeMs: STALE_RUN_TMP_MAX_AGE_MS` and `now` equal to the value `_runTmpCloseDeps.now()` returns.
`closeRunTmp({ runId: "r1", dryRun: true })` calls neither `_runTmpCloseDeps.wipeRunTmp` nor `_runTmpCloseDeps.sweepStaleRunTmpRoots`.
When `_runTmpCloseDeps.sweepStaleRunTmpRoots` rejects, `closeRunTmp` resolves and logs one warn entry.
When `_runTmpCloseDeps.wipeRunTmp` rejects, `closeRunTmp` still calls `_runTmpCloseDeps.sweepStaleRunTmpRoots`.
With `_runtimeTmpDeps.closeRunTmp` stubbed, `createRuntime(config, workdir)` followed by `runtime.close()` calls the stub once with `{ runId: runtime.runId, dryRun: false }`.
With `_runtimeTmpDeps.closeRunTmp` stubbed, calling `runtime.close()` twice on one runtime calls the stub exactly once.
With `_runtimeTmpDeps.closeRunTmp` stubbed, `createRuntime(config, workdir, { dryRun: true })` followed by `runtime.close()` calls the stub with `dryRun: true`.
With `_runtimeTmpDeps.closeRunTmp` stubbed and the runtime's MCP pool `close` rejecting, `runtime.close()` still calls the stub once.
With `_runtimeTmpDeps.closeRunTmp` stubbed and a run memory passed in `opts.memory`, `runtime.close()` calls the stub after the memory's `close`.

With `_runtimeTmpDeps.closeRunTmp` left as its default and only `_runTmpCloseDeps.wipeRunTmp` and `_runTmpCloseDeps.sweepStaleRunTmpRoots` stubbed, `createRuntime(config, workdir)` followed by `runtime.close()` calls `wipeRunTmp` with `runtime.runId` and calls `sweepStaleRunTmpRoots` with `currentRunId: runtime.runId`.

routing.reasoning: Two small new modules and a single call in the existing runtime teardown finally, all using the repo's injectable _deps idiom; no new abstractions, so one tdd-simple session suffices.

modifiedFiles.reason: add one override, `_runTmpCloseDeps.sweepStaleRunTmpRoots = async () => {}`, beside the existing real-host dep overrides, so the tests that close a real runtime (the shared runtime test helper, the run-setup, plan, bot and runtime suites) never list or sweep the developer's real temp parent.

userStories.title: Removed-key warnings for the curator and the #2832 keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the 15 paths in the table below to `REMOVED_CONFIG_KEYS` with the two new hints, and delete `migrateLegacyNonBlockingFix` and its call in `compat-shims.ts`.

**Motivation** — Setting any of these keys does nothing, while `nax config` and the schema still present them as live settings; the owner's global config sets three of them, and the curator appends to a global JSONL file on every run.

**Approach** — New entries in `REMOVED_CONFIG_KEYS`. The strip runs before `NaxConfigSchema.safeParse` at all three loader sites, so a config that sets these keys loads and warns once per key: `Config key "<path>" has been removed — <hint>. Remove it from your config.`

| Path | Hint |
|:--|:--|
| `curator` | `CURATOR_REMOVED_HINT` = `the curator feature was removed; nax no longer writes ~/.nax/global/curator, which is safe to delete` |
| `quality.testing` | `TESTING_POLICY_HINT` = `nothing reads this key since pipeline mode was removed; state test and mocking policy in a .nax/rules file` |
| `prompts.behavioralGuardrails` | `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT` |
| `review.nonBlockingFix` | `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT` |
| `review.adversarial.nonBlockingFix` | `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT` |
| `review.parseRetryMaxAttempts` | `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT` |
| `review.conflictDetection` | `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT` |
| `review.semantic.demandInspectionTrail` | `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT` |
| `review.semantic.acRegroundOnDrop` | `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT` |
| `review.semantic.recurrenceDemotion` | `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT` |
| `review.adversarial.demandInspectionTrail` | `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT` |
| `review.adversarial.acRegroundOnDrop` | `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT` |
| `review.adversarial.recurrenceDemotion` | `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT` |
| `review.adversarial.parallel` | `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT` |
| `review.adversarial.maxConcurrentSessions` | `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT` |

`migrateLegacyNonBlockingFix` (`config/migrations.ts`, called from `compat-shims.ts:499`) copied `review.adversarial.nonBlockingFix` to `review.nonBlockingFix` with a deprecation warning. Both paths are now removed keys, so this story deletes the shim and its call. A config that sets the legacy path gets the one removed-key warning and never the deprecation warning.

Failure handling: config sets a removed key -> one removed-key warning per path; config loads.

**Scope** — In: `REMOVED_CONFIG_KEYS` entries, the two hint constants, shim deletion, the listed test updates. Out: deleting the schema fields, types, defaults and `nax config` descriptions for these keys (US-006); deleting the curator feature itself (US-005). Also out: stripping keys from `~/.nax/config.json`, profiles or this repo's `.nax/config.json`.

**Interface**
```typescript
// packages/nax/src/config/removed-config-keys.ts
export const CURATOR_REMOVED_HINT: string;
export const TESTING_POLICY_HINT: string;
// REMOVED_CONFIG_KEYS: baseline = existing C1 entries; target = same entries plus the 15 above
// stripKeysAtPaths(conf, keys, warn?) and PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT are read, not changed
```
acceptanceCriteria: Loading a raw config `{ curator: { enabled: true } }` through `stripRemovedConfigKeys` with a warn sink yields a result with no `curator` key and exactly one warning equal to `Config key "curator" has been removed — ${CURATOR_REMOVED_HINT}. Remove it from your config.`
`CURATOR_REMOVED_HINT` imported from `config/removed-config-keys` equals `the curator feature was removed; nax no longer writes ~/.nax/global/curator, which is safe to delete`.

Loading `{ quality: { testing: { hermetic: true, mockGuidance: "x" } } }` through `stripRemovedConfigKeys` yields a `quality` object with no `testing` key and exactly one warning naming `quality.testing` with `TESTING_POLICY_HINT`.
`TESTING_POLICY_HINT` equals `nothing reads this key since pipeline mode was removed; state test and mocking policy in a .nax/rules file`.
Loading `{ prompts: { behavioralGuardrails: "strict" } }` through `stripRemovedConfigKeys` yields exactly one warning naming `prompts.behavioralGuardrails` with `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT`.

Loading `{ review: { nonBlockingFix: { enabled: true } } }` through `stripRemovedConfigKeys` yields a `review` object with no `nonBlockingFix` key and exactly one warning naming `review.nonBlockingFix`.

Loading `{ review: { parseRetryMaxAttempts: 5, conflictDetection: { maxOscillations: 3 } } }` through `stripRemovedConfigKeys` yields exactly two warnings, one naming `review.parseRetryMaxAttempts` and one naming `review.conflictDetection`.

Loading a `review.semantic` object that sets `demandInspectionTrail`, `acRegroundOnDrop` and `recurrenceDemotion` through `stripRemovedConfigKeys` yields exactly three warnings, one per `review.semantic.<key>` path.

Loading a `review.adversarial` object that sets `demandInspectionTrail`, `acRegroundOnDrop`, `recurrenceDemotion`, `parallel` and `maxConcurrentSessions` through `stripRemovedConfigKeys` yields exactly five warnings, one per `review.adversarial.<key>` path.
Loading `{ review: { adversarial: { enabled: true, parallel: true } } }` through `stripRemovedConfigKeys` keeps `review.adversarial.enabled` equal to `true`.

Loading a project config file that sets `review.adversarial.nonBlockingFix: { enabled: true }` through the config loader produces exactly one warning naming `review.adversarial.nonBlockingFix` with `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT`.
Loading a project config file that sets `review.adversarial.nonBlockingFix` through the config loader produces no warning containing `is deprecated`.

Loading a project config file that sets `curator: { enabled: true }` and `disabledPlugins: ["curator"]` through the config loader produces exactly one removed-key warning naming `curator`, and the resolved `disabledPlugins` still equals `["curator"]`.

routing.reasoning: Table-driven additions to an existing mechanism plus one shim deletion; several existing tests need updating.

modifiedFiles.reason: the test "REMOVED_CONFIG_KEYS is exactly the closed set of keys C1 removed" (around line 592) pins the key list; extend the expected list with the 15 new paths and retitle it to the closed set of removed keys.
the assertion that `prompts.behavioralGuardrails` produces no warning (around line 212) is replaced: it now produces exactly one removed-key warning with `PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT`.
the `migrateLegacyNonBlockingFix` cases are deleted with the shim; the invariant moves to the new removed-key test (one removed-key warning, no deprecation warning).
assertions that `review.nonBlockingFix` parses, defaults or is aliased from `review.adversarial.nonBlockingFix` are deleted or inverted: both paths are now stripped with one removed-key warning each.

analysis:
Four cleanups shipped together (closes #2860, #2861, #2832, #2830). All stories are scoped to packages/nax.

Key files: execution/lifecycle/run-tmp-wipe.ts (wipeRunTmp, _runTmpWipeDeps {remove, exists}); runtime/index.ts (createRuntime / closeRuntime finally, ~line 419; close() is memoised via teardown; already imports ../execution/pid-registry by file path); packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/session-tmp.ts:89 (runTmpRoot, exported from @nathapp/nax-agent, sanitises the runId and applies trust checks); execution/lifecycle/run-cleanup.ts:381-394 (second wipe, removed in US-006); config/removed-config-keys.ts:91 (REMOVED_CONFIG_KEYS, stripKeysAtPaths, PIPELINE_ONLY_KEY_HINT; strip runs before NaxConfigSchema.safeParse at three loader sites); config/migrations.ts + config/compat-shims.ts:499 (migrateLegacyNonBlockingFix); context/engine/providers/static-rules.ts:139 (ruleMatchesStage), :248-253 (stage filter), :267 (warnOnAppliesToStageContradiction call); context/rules/rules-frontmatter.ts:228 (extractStages, KNOWN_VALID_STAGES, EXTRA_KNOWN_STAGES, STAGE_CONTEXT_MAP import); cli/rules-lint.ts:324-330 (re-emits rule.warnings, needs no change); plugins/loader.ts:139 (built-in registration); bin/nax.ts (curator command registration); runtime/paths.ts (curatorRollupPath); plugins/extensions.ts (run-end context).

Dependency order: US-001 -> US-002; US-003 -> US-005; US-004 independent; US-006 is terminal and depends on US-002..US-005 (deletion only: schema/types/defaults for #2832 keys, stages fields, second wipe in cleanupRun, runtimeRunId option).

Risks: (1) removeRunTmpTree must never chmod symlinks or paths outside the root (use lstat, never follow). (2) test/preload.ts must stub _runTmpCloseDeps.sweepStaleRunTmpRoots to a no-op or tests closing a real runtime would sweep the developer's real temp parent. (3) runtime/index.ts must import the lifecycle modules by file path, never via the lifecycle barrel (cycle risk; package-boundary checks). (4) Until US-006, both wipes run; the second sees an absent root and logs at debug. (5) US-005 and US-006 are wide deletions; typecheck and lint in packages/nax are the removal checks, and scripts/check-worktree-id-ssot.ts plus the complexity and test-escape-hatches baselines must be edited by hand (never re-baseline coverage or run --update-baseline). (6) The disabledPlugins list naming curator stays harmless. (7) The existing test 'REMOVED_CONFIG_KEYS is exactly the closed set of keys C1 removed' pins the list and must be extended. (8) extractStages still validates shape (list of non-empty strings, else RulesFrontmatterError) and stages stays in KNOWN_FRONTMATTER_KEYS. (9) STAGE_CONTEXT_MAP and context.v2.stages stay. (10) Repo .nax/ is read-only to the run: do not edit .nax/rules or .nax/config.json.

Notable tests: test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-tmp-wipe.test.ts, test/integration/execution/lifecycle/run-tmp-wipe.test.ts (listed by name in the confined integration-hygiene suite; keep path), test/unit/runtime/runtime-close-partial.test.ts, test/unit/config/removed-config-keys*.test.ts, test/unit/cli/rules-lint.test.ts, static-rules-*.test.ts, rules-frontmatter.test.ts. Existing code uses injectable _deps objects; follow that idiom. User style: immutability, no emojis, small files.
outOfScope: Wiping each session's temp directory when that session closes (per-session wipe from the #2860 comment): ruled out 2026-11-11, because a re-dispatched session with the same name would lose its temp files mid-run.
`nax chat` sessions: they do not create run temp roots (they never pass a `runId` to `resolveDispatchLauncher`), so this feature does not change chat.
Wiring `quality.testing` (hermetic requirement, `externalBoundaries`, `mockGuidance`) into workflow prompts: ruled out 2026-11-11; the key is stripped, and test policy belongs in `.nax/rules/`.
Mapping rule `stages:` to workflow role names: ruled out 2026-11-11 in favour of retiring the key.
Shrinking `STAGE_CONTEXT_MAP` or the `context.v2.stages` config: they key per-stage context budgets, not rule selection.
Deleting existing `~/.nax/global/curator/` data: nax stops writing it and leaves it in place.
Removing `stages:` lines from this repo's `.nax/rules/*.md` and the `curator` key from this repo's `.nax/config.json`: `.nax/` is read-only to the run, so the owner does both by hand after merge.

Stripping the removed keys from `~/.nax/config.json`, profiles and other projects' configs: the owner does it with the config-key-removal runbook and updates `~/.nax/scripts/strip-removed-config-keys.py`.
nax-toolkit skill updates (`rules-setup` references `curator.md`; `nax-run-telemetry` reads the curator rollup): a follow-up in the skills repo.
Removing a stale root that another OS user owns: `runTmpRoot` already falls back to a per-user parent, and the sweep only lists the parent this user's runs resolve to.
